Under Henry Ford II's leadership, the company launched successful models like the Thunderbird (1954) and the Mustang (1964). But this period also saw the introduction of the Edsel (model years 1958–60), a notable fiasco that made the name “Edsel” a synonym for failure. Henry Ford II guided the company as chief executive officer from 1945 to 1970 and as chair of the board from 1960 to 1980.

## 1970s–2000s: Diversification and strategic acquisitions [...] In the 1950s and '60s, Ford Motor Company began a phase of limited diversification, highlighted by its purchase of the electronics company Philco in 1961. But by the 1990s, Ford had refocused attention on its automotive concerns and financial services. results.title: China approves Geely acquisition of 34% of Ford España | live
results.content:
BEIJING, Oct 12 (Reuters) - China's market regulator has unconditionally approved Geely's acquisition of 34% of Ford Motor's Spanish subsidiary Ford España, it said on Monday.

In July the companies said Geely would build two electric SUVs at Ford’s factory in Valencia, Spain, and they would together develop a vehicle under a newly formed joint venture.

The JV is to be 66% owned by Ford and 34% owned by Geely, the companies added. [...] Euronext and Nord Pool, the European power exchange, announced the launch of a dedicated Nordic and Baltic power futures market.
